summary: Build workplace injury response skills with assessment, bleeding control, and handover practice. Enrol your team in a 5-day course.
lede: Medical response to occupational injuries covers assessing an injured worker, stabilizing immediate risks, and deciding when to escalate. It is for workplace health, safety, first-aid, and site personnel who may need to act before a clinician arrives, with practice in scene surveys, bleeding control, CPR-AED and injury care, plus patient handover and incident documentation.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals who need to make fast, defensible medical response decisions for workplace injuries and medical incidents.
prerequisites: Prerequisites required: working knowledge of workplace safety procedures and emergency contacts; no clinical qualification is required, but prior first-aid exposure is helpful. Participants should bring a laptop or tablet for digital incident log practice, and should be prepared to work through scenario worksheets, injury assessment forms, and response templates. Coding is not required. The course teaches advanced response concepts at an operational level, with hands-on practice in assessment, stabilization, escalation, and reporting rather than clinical diagnosis.
